Asylum

/uh-SY-lum/ — rhymes with 'why'-lum · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Asylum is official protection or safe shelter given to someone fleeing harm.

After receiving death threats for her reporting, the journalist was granted asylum in Canada.

Worked Example

When soldiers began arresting journalists in her country, Nadia fled across the border with only a backpack. Officials interviewed her, reviewed the danger she faced back home, and granted her permission to stay under the host country's protection.

Nadia received asylum — official protection from harm for someone fleeing danger. Unlike a simple 'shelter,' which is any place that keeps out weather or trouble, asylum is formal protection, often granted by a government to people escaping persecution.

How Asylum Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

refuge

refuge: a safe place away from danger

sanctuary

sanctuary: a protected place where no one can harm you

haven

haven: a place of safety and rest

Antonyms

danger

danger: the possibility of being harmed

exposure

exposure: the state of being left unprotected

How Strong Is It? — shelter → asylum → immunity

shelter vs. asylum

shelter vs. asylum: Shelter is weaker than asylum — any roof or cover can be a shelter, but asylum is formal protection from persecution, often granted by a government.

immunity vs. asylum

immunity vs. asylum: Immunity is stronger than asylum — it removes a threat entirely and permanently, while asylum protects you only within your place of safety.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of asylum.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — a-

prefix — a-: without, not (Greek)

root — sylum

root — sylum: right of seizure (from Greek sylon; an asylon was 'a place safe from seizure')

Put it together

Put it together: Greek asylon meant 'a place without seizure' — a- (without) + sylon (the right to seize someone), spelled -sylum in English. A place where no one could be captured naturally became a place of protection.

Use the root in a new word: atypical
